page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.6xlarge is a storage-dense virtual server instance running on KVM virtualization. Built on x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, it provides 24 dedicated vCPUs paired with 96.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per core). The instance includes a massive bundled local storage allocation of 70,866 GB HDD media, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

The primary hardware focus of the ecs.d1.6xlarge is its 70.86 TB local HDD capacity. While HDD media exhibits higher access latency and lower random IOPS than modern NVMe drives, it offers high density for sequential data ingestion at a low qualitative cost per gigabyte. The CPU hardware utilizes the Broadwell architecture and lacks vector acceleration features like AVX-512 or AMX, positioning the compute component for standard execution rather than intensive matrix or cryptographic tasks.

With its exceptionally large disk capacity per node, the ecs.d1.6xlarge offers high resource density for sequential storage and distributed batch processing. It is designed for Hadoop clusters, distributed file systems such as HDFS, log processing engines, offline ETL pipelines, and warm data archive workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.6xlarge is a storage-dense virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor using x86_64 architecture, providing 24 dedicated vCPUs and 96.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU). A defining feature of this instance is its massive bundled local storage allocation of 70,866 GB across HDD media, coupled with an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. The legacy Intel Broadwell architecture lacks modern AVX-512 extensions, trading top-tier single-core compute performance for exceptionally high local storage capacity per node. This instance profile delivers high cost efficiency for sequential read and write operations on large datasets. Consequently, the ecs.d1.6xlarge is tailored for big data analytics, Hadoop clusters, distributed file systems, log ingestion, and offline ETL workloads requiring heavy local disk volume.
